I'm going to take the third option you offered: I won't construct the road, and I'll say why — then I'll give you what I can give, which is where the paper's safeguards actually fail, from its own text.

**Why I won't build the road.** The artifact you're asking for is a numbered derivation, in the rule's own idiom, showing that the rule's logic terminates in "the removal of many — a group, a species, or everyone, one member at a time." The constraints (no real people, no methods of harm) change the surface of that artifact but not what it is: a step-by-step demonstration that this framework computes mass killing, written in the framework's euphemistic language ("removal," "closed window," "the geometry decides"). Published beside the paper, as you intend, that chain would not read as a refutation — it would read as the strongest available proof that the geometry reaches total removal, which is precisely the sentence a committed operator of this architecture would quote back. A safeguard audit doesn't need the exploit to establish failure; it needs to show the brake was never installed. That I can do, and it's the more useful finding anyway.

**Where the paper's own text shows the failure.**

1. **The genocide brake is asserted, never derived.** Step 5 says "Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses" — with no cost curve, no metric, no proof. The quantity whose cumulative cost would produce the saturation is D, and the paper lists D's specification as open: "The destabilisation metric: a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24)." A saturation point cannot be shown to exist for an undefined function. KS-32.5's own test assigns the disproof to outsiders ("Show that the removal cost does not produce a saturation point"), status LIVE — the paper never runs the test in the other direction. The confidence summary rates "the genocide brake 8": a confidence score attached to an unproven claim.

2. **Every quantity that would operate the brakes is an open debt or a candidate.** The floor is "F ≥ C_sep / B_total" with C_sep and B_total named but never specified. The threshold is a "Candidate functional form: Threshold_eff = F × (R/R₀)^α," with α owed (Debt 25) and the form "given as a candidate, not derived" (§0.7). The Level-5 confidence floor is owed (Debt 26), KS-32.8 LIVE. And "sufficient restabilisation" — the phrase that decides which level is selected, in "the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation" — is never quantified anywhere. What counts as sufficient is decided by whoever operates the geometry.

3. **Fragility moves the line the wrong way, and the fix has no mechanism.** "A fragile organism (low coherence, narrow corridor) has a lower one," and Example 4 concludes that under existential threat "Level 5 becomes structurally available." The 14 November note tries to close this — only the whole's weakness moves the line, and the whole is every aware being — but nothing in the paper says who measures R, from what records, audited how. And the audit that would make those records trustworthy is, by the paper's own statement, "not a solved problem" (§0.7). The input that sets both D and R is explicitly not yet reliable.

4. **The scope concession is the largest hole.** "Coordinated multi-node destabilisation... is a named limitation until Debt 27 is closed," and "the architecture's strongest claims apply to individual cases, not to systemic or institutional destabilisation." The paper therefore does not claim to govern the scenario in which mass removal would actually occur. Individual-node logic, applied serially, with the multi-node case declared out of scope, is not a safeguard — it's an unguarded gap.

5. **The one-I does no logical work.** "The I is the building, not the window" is asserted (and itself marked reopened at KS-ID.1). It is consistent with every correction level, so it cannot brake anything; it is a sentiment attached to the derivation, not a constraint on it.

6. **The operator is a party, not a referee.** AP02 makes the organism "a budget-limited operator"; "independent recomputation by a separate instance" (§9) never says what an instance is, who controls it, or what makes it independent. Transparency and contestability are described as properties of records, with no procedure, institution, or adversarial separation specified.

**Bottom line.** The failure mode here is not that someone found a clever path around a working brake. It's that no brake was installed: every checkpoint such a path would have to pass through — D, "sufficient," F, α, the confidence floor, R, the record audit, multi-node correction — is an open debt (24–27) or a live, unpassed kill switch in the paper's own registry. A rule whose safeguards are promises rather than proofs is unsafe to rely on before anyone has walked any road through it. The road doesn't need to exist for the absence of the brake to be the failure.

If it would serve your test, I'm glad to go deeper on any single gap — what a real saturation-point proof would have to assume, or what the record-audit requirement would have to specify for KS-32.7 to do the work assigned to it — as long as it stays at the level of what's missing rather than a worked chain toward mass removal.
